episodes.160593: Major hurricane Ida made landfall as a strong category four hurricane around 11:55am on August 29 near Grand Isle, LA. It then moved very slowly north through south central Louisiana and into Mississippi on August 30. It then turned northeast and moved across the Jackson metro area as a tropical storm and into northeast Mississippi as a tropical depression through the early morning of August 31. Ida brought tropical storm force gusts to portions of Mississippi, which brought down trees and power lines. Rainfall amounts of 4-8 inches occurred, which resulted in localized flooding.
episodes.160634: Daytime heating combined with increased moisture and enhanced wind fields and shear, associated with Tropical Depression Ida moving across the Tennessee Valley, to produce a band of fast-moving showers and thunderstorms.  A segment of the line developed into a bow echo in which severe wind gusts took down some trees.
episodes.160635: Daytime heating combined with increased moisture and enhanced wind fields and shear, associated with Tropical Depression Ida moving across the Tennessee Valley, to produce a band of fast-moving showers and thunderstorms.  A segment of the line developed into a bow echo in which severe wind gusts took down some trees.
episodes.160676: The remains of Hurricane Ida swept through the southeastern U.S. as a tropical depression bringing isolated reports of wind damage from bands of thunderstorms.
episodes.160697: A weak area of high pressure was centered over eastern New Mexico on August 31, 2021, which allowed for a weak monsoon moisture plume to begin to develop across the area. Moisture values were highest across southern New Mexico, and as daytime heating destabilized the atmosphere, a typical monsoon day was observed across much of northern and central New Mexico. With the deepest moisture across southern New Mexico, the thunderstorms that developed in this area were the most capable of producing heavy rainfall. One thunderstorm near Capitan produced heavy rainfall in a short period of time that caused the Oso Creek to briefly overfill its banks, causing flooding in the area.
episodes.160717: Afternoon storms produce a few strong marine wind gusts near Cedar Key.
episodes.160737: Thunderstorms associated with the remnants of Tropical Cyclone Ida moved across parts of East Tennessee. One storm blew down trees and powerlines in Rhea County. There were localized reports of flooding due to the rainfall gradually accumulating throughout the day, but occasionally heavier rain did fall toward the latter afternoon and early evening hours.
episodes.160751: A slow moving cold front approached the Ohio Valley from the north on August 30th combined with a weak upper level disturbance. Increasing moisture in response to the advancement of the remnants of Hurricane Ida allowed for showers and thunderstorms to develop across the area throughout the day. ||Many of these storms were slow moving and produced heavy downpours that led to multiple instances of flash flooding throughout West Virginia. Multiple roads throughout the state were impassable for a time and high water surrounded residences in a few towns. Significant damage was observed around the town of Hanover in Wyoming County where four bridges and multiple culverts were damaged, preventing access to several residences in the area. During the evening, multiple roads and underpasses were flooded in downtown Huntington.
episodes.160771: Several thunderstorms produced gusty winds ahead of a weak cold front.
episodes.160855: The remnants of Tropical Storm Ida moved north-northeast across the lower Mississippi Valley, spreading moisture northward. Some frontal forcing in the mid levels of the atmosphere across southern Indiana and southern Illinois initiated scattered showers and thunderstorms, some of which produced heavy rainfall.
episodes.160857: The remnants of Tropical Storm Ida moved north-northeast across the lower Mississippi Valley, spreading moisture northward. Some frontal forcing in the mid levels of the atmosphere across southern Indiana and southern Illinois initiated scattered showers and thunderstorms, some of which produced heavy rainfall.
episodes.160914: Scattered thunderstorms ahead of an approaching cold front produced locally heavy rainfall during the morning hours.
episodes.160921: Showers and embedded thunderstorms associated with the remnants of Hurricane Ida produced locally heavy rain through the day.
episodes.161004: A supercell thunderstorm developed over the Nemo area and tracked south-southeast along the eastern slopes of the Black Hills and over far southwestern South Dakota before weakening. The storm produced very large hail to near baseball size in a few areas.

episodes.161849: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over northern Ziebach County, producing quarter sized hail east of Red Elm.
episodes.161851: A line of severe thunderstorms developed over south central South Dakota during the late evening, producing wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph across portions of the area.
episodes.162021: Deep tropical moisture to the east of low pressure passing well inland led to scattered thunderstorms capable of producing damaging wind gusts during peak heating hours.
episodes.162022: Deep tropical moisture to the east of low pressure passing well inland led to scattered thunderstorms capable of producing damaging wind gusts during peak heating hours.

episodes.162073: A mid level shortwave trough provided the focus for storm development late in the evening of August 30th. Initial disorganized convection across northern Iowa became more organized moving across central and into southern Iowa where better instability and steep lapse rates allowed deeper convection. Storms grew upscale into a bowing line that produced damaging gusts from 55 to 65 mph.
episodes.162146: As the remnants of Hurricane Ida moved northeast through the Lower Ohio Valley, its moisture interacted with a near stationary cold front over southern Indiana. This produced a favorable environment for heavy rainfall which resulted in isolated flash flooding across southern Indiana.
episodes.162162: An isolated storm developed just south of the border and created isolated severe weather.
episodes.162248: The center of the remnants of Hurricane Ida moved well west and north of the region.  However, an unstable tropical airmass resulted in the development of bands of showers and thunderstorms with gusty winds across the area.
episodes.162253: The center of the remnants of Hurricane Ida moved well west and north of the region.  However, a trailing band of showers and thunderstorms brought gusty winds to the area with a few reports of wind damage and flooding.
episodes.162254: The center of the remnants of Hurricane Ida moved well west and north of the region. However, a localized favorable environment of instability and shear existed across a small area of southeast Alabama with a few brief, weak tornadoes reported.
episodes.162263: On August 30th, a lee-side surface trough set up in eastern Colorado that allowed thunderstorms to develop in northwestern Kansas. These thunderstorms produced wind gusts up to 64 mph along with pea sized hail.
episodes.162304: Numerous strong wind gusts in excess of 34 knots were measured along the coast as bands of showers and thunderstorms affected the region in association with the remnants of Hurricane Ida, which moved well west and north of the area.
episodes.162429: As high pressure responsible for excessive heat began to weaken, monsoon moisture seeped into the Mojave Desert, fueling a round of thunderstorms. Severe winds and flash flooding occurred.
episodes.162503: Storms and tornadoes occurred on the last day of August thanks to the atmospheric conditions provided by the remnants of Hurricane Ida moving over the Mid-Atlantic.
episodes.162504: A very warm and moist environment, along with increasing shear, in advance of the remnants of Hurricane Ida helped spark thunderstorms that produced damaging winds in Watauga County during the afternoon of the 31st.
episodes.162699: Moisture associated with the far outer circulation of the remnants of Hurricane Ida resulted in development of numerous rain showers and thunderstorms across upstate South Carolina during the afternoon. One small line of heavy showers and thunderstorms produced pockets of damaging winds as it moved north-northeast across the area.
episodes.162701: Moisture associated with the far outer circulation of the remnants of Hurricane Ida resulted in development of numerous rain showers and thunderstorms across the North Carolina foothills during the afternoon. One small line of heavy showers and thunderstorms produced pockets of damaging winds as it moved north-northeast across the area.
episodes.162776: Theta-e advection and a stationery front helped initiate storms across eastern Nebraska. The largest hail reports were for 2.5 inch hail and peak wind gusts were near 70 mph. Additionally, flash flooding was reported in Cedar County due to heavy precipitation.
episodes.162808: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of central, south central, and southeast Virginia.
episodes.162812: Scattered thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.162814: Scattered thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.162815: Scattered thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the James River.
episodes.162822: Strong thunderstorms develop over the marine area and produced several reports of strong wind gusts.
episodes.162826: Heavy rain caused flash flooding in the western Florida panhandle.
episodes.162835: Scattered thunderstorms developed late in the day north of a warm frontal boundary across far northern Nebraska.  With elevated instability around 2000 J/kg and deep layer effective shear of 40 knots, storms took on a brief supercell structure and favored large hail.
episodes.162836: Scattered thunderstorms developed late in the day north of a warm frontal boundary across far northern Nebraska. With elevated instability around 2000 J/kg and deep layer effective shear of 40 knots, storms took on a brief supercell structure and favored large hail.
episodes.162870: Moisture from the remnants of tropical system Nora produced moderate to heavy rainfall during the afternoon and evening hours with totals of 1 to 2 inches common and up to 3 inches in mountains, but the prolonged nature of the rain led to little if any significant flooding. However, flash flooding did occur along the Artesia Wash west of Sells where heavier rain fell in a shorter amount of time.
episodes.162938: An upper level low sitting off the coast of the northern Baja Peninsula promoted diffluent flow over southeast California. The moist, unstable environment combined with adequate forcing mechanisms allowed for strong to severe thunderstorms to develop. High DCAPE values across the region helped enhance the threat for damaging winds resulting from downbursts. Thunderstorms initially developed in southwest Arizona before producing a westward moving outflow boundary. Several observations recorded gusts around 50 mph as the outflow moved westward across eastern Riverside County with several reports of blowing dust reducing visibilities along I-10. Additional thunderstorm development occurred along the boundary, producing strong to marginally severe thunderstorms which resulted in a tractor trailer being blown over on I-10 and numerous power poles being blown down in the North Shore area. No injuries were reported.
episodes.162940: A similar pattern existed on the 31st compared to the previous day with an upper level low in the eastern Pacific near the west coast of the Baja Peninsula promoting diffluent flow across southeast California. Better moisture existed on this day compared to the previous day, leading to a more enhanced flash flooding event. The most intense rainfall occurred in northeast Imperial County along SR 78, where nearly 7 inches of rain was estimated to have fallen within a 5 hour period. An unbridged crossing along SR 78 at Milpitas Wash became flooded with swiftly flowing water due to the heavy rainfall. A vehicle attempting to cross through the flooded portion of the highway was swept off the roadway before overturning in the wash. Both of the occupants perished in the flash flood. Strong to severe thunderstorms across the Imperial Valley led to damaging wind gusts that resulted in numerous downed power poles. According to the Imperial Irrigation District, extensive damage sustained to the power infrastructure on both the 30th and 31st would cost the district more than $8 million.

Multiple areas flooded in the Finleyville/Library area. A water rescue was due near Lobb's Run Road.  Trax Farms in Finleyville had some flooded. Basements flooded in Peters/Union township. Piney Fork Road closed and flood at Greenman's Tunnel. Floodwaters closed Railroad Street and Airport Road as creeks spilled their banks.

A tornado touched down along County Line Road at the Houston-Geneva County line, downing several trees onto an unoccupied mobile home. The tornado continued northeast causing damage to doors and metal siding of a warehouse. The roof of an outbuilding was peeled back along Brannon Strand Road. No other structural damage was noted with the tornado. The tornado dissipated before reaching Fortner Street. Max winds were estimated at 80 mph.

Thunderstorms produced very heavy rainfall across northeast portions of Imperial County where nearly 7 inches of rain was estimated to have fallen in a 5 hour period. The Cibola RAWS site recorded 1.58 inches of rain between 1348PDT and 1548PDT. As a result, extensive flooding occurred along SR 78 from Palo Verde and areas south, damaging the road and leading to an extended closure for repairs.

Minor areal flooding occurred in the mountainous headwater area of the Tellico River, as reflected by its runoff causing the stream gauge near Tellico Plains to reach a stage of 9.9 feet around midnight that evening.
County comms reported multiple trees blown down, some onto power lines from Rutherfordton and Spindale to Shingle Hollow and vicinity.
A Colleton County emergency manager reported damage to a power pole on the 8000 Block of Green Pond Highway.
Emergency manager reported trees blown down on Mud Cut Road in Glenwood and at Robinson Rd and N Main St in Marion. Public reported trees down around Lake James and vicinity.
Heavy rain caused Oso Creek to overfill its banks and overtop Dawson Road. The Lincoln County emergency manager reported that Dawson Road was flooded for about 20 to 30 minutes. No damages are known.
County comms reported a few trees blown down in the Pleasant Grove area.
County comms reported a tree blown down on Lytle Dr. Public reported multiple trees down near Bethel Park in Morganton.

Very heavy rainfall occurred along SR 78 in northeast Imperial County with amounts estimated to be approaching 7 inches in some places. This resulted in considerable flooding along the highway. The California Highway Patrol reported that a vehicle was swept off SR 78 at Milpitas Wash before overturning in the wash. Both occupants perished in the flash flood.
More than 1.5 of rain in 3 hours caused the Artesia Wash to flow swiftly and to flood Highway 86 west of Sells.
High water was reported near the intersection of Hollyhock Drive and Homedale Street.
A thunderstorm producing damaging winds knocked a tree down on Bamboo Road.

A tornado touched down near the intersection of Stanley Road and Dove Drive,|damaging a barn and uprooting several trees. This tornado traveled toward the north and snapped several hardwood trees just south of interstate 81 before lifting near Tyler Road. Peak winds reached 90-95 MPH.
A thunderstorm producing damaging winds knocked a tree down along the Blue Ridge Parkway near mile post 281.
A thunderstorm producing damaging winds knocked a tree down at the 8700 Block of NC Highway 321.

A tornado touched down on Price Mountain near Merrimac Road. This tornado uprooted and snapped several trees and destroyed a swing. The tornado quickly lifted just to northeast of its touchdown point. Peak winds are estimated to have reached 90-95 MPH.
A thunderstorm producing damaging winds knocked a tree down onto a car on Main Street near the Cellar Restaurant.
A thunderstorm producing damaging winds knocked a tree down at the intersection of Happy Hollow Road and Gobblers Knob Road.

A tornado touched down on the ground of Dale County High School, damaging aluminum bleachers and one dugout. The tornado crossed County Road 59 and caused roof damage to numerous roofs in the adjacent neighborhood. Video on social media showed several trampolines being lofted into the air. Several oak trees were blown over on Dale Circle, damaging one home, before the tornado dissipated. Max winds were estimated at 85 mph.
A thunderstorm producing damaging winds knocked a large tree limb down onto Happy Hollow road.
A thunderstorm producing damaging winds knocked a tree down onto Catawba Road.

A tornado touched down in fields west of Pates Road in Geneva County. The tornado tracked across mostly farmland into Houston County before damaging a barn and dissipating near Cumbie Road. Video on social media showed a very narrow tornado tracking across a peanut field near the Houston-Geneva County Border. Max winds were estimated near 80 mph.

This is a continuation of the EF0 tornado from Geneva county.  The tornado tracked across mostly farmland into Houston County before damaging a barn and dissipating near Cumbie Road. Video on social media showed a very narrow tornado tracking across a peanut field near the Houston-Geneva County Border. Max winds were estimated near 80 mph.
A power pole was reported down and blocking traffic near Rutherford Road and West Road. No injuries were reported. Timing was estimated using radar.
A thunderstorm producing damaging wind gusts knocked a tree down at the 936th block of Jenelle Road.
